item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's less edgelordy in-and-of-itself and more edgelord-bait.

I posted this originally on reddit, but it's my analysis of the mystique of 049.

+ show block
– hide block

Here's what 049 does right: It's a mysterious "intellectual" character that does not rely on brute force to be scary and powerful. Despite this power, 049 is not a Mary Sue, is contained by the Foundation, and believes in some code that prevents it from simply deciding everyone needs to die. In addition, it's got a way cool, sleek, sinister look in its photo.

Why does this matter? Let's say you're a teenage boy. You're trying to find relevance in your life. You aren't physically dominant, so you're losing that popularity game, and you see people failing at what they say they're doing all around you, and you want to fight back against that. None of this is bad; it's all normal and a part of growing up. I've been that, myself. Disillusionment is setting in, replacing childhood wonder, so you're trying to balance neat new ideas with the grittiness you see around you.

Enter 049. He talks, he thinks. He sees the corruption and decay around him, and he wants to deliver a solution, save the world. He's not physical, but he is overpowering. Finally, he's mysterious. You don't know what exactly his "disease" he treats is… but you've got some ideas.

049 is an excellent role model for the power fantasy of a typical teenager in this case. He's not super fast, or super strong. He's not even super smart (he calls himself a doctor, but other than knowing how to turn a corpse into a zombie, shows no extra specialized knowledge). So, he's relatable. He's someone you can see yourself being, and his "disease" can be whatever you want it to be, so he's fighting the evil you envision around you. And, importantly, he's feared.

Now the problem from the point of view of a veteran author is that a power-fantasy character only really makes sense in a vacuum. Something has to change in order for the character to make sense as a part of the larger world. 049 can't only interact with foils. Also, the writing for the 049 article isn't that good, honestly. It's good at exuding cool, but that's really about it. And once you reach a certain age… you'll have seen that cool in so many ways, in so many settings, that you look past it all and wonder if there's something nuanced, something complex under that surface to keep using and building upon.

Because think about it: How does 049 compare to Darth Vader? To Lord Soth? To Drizzt Do'Urden? To Deadpool? To Wolverine? Strip away the common cool, and most of these characters still have backstories, personalities, moods, actions that still speak to them. 049 has… zombies.

049 is an important character in the Foundation canon. I think he definitely still has a place, and I want to keep him around for that. But he's not deep or all that interesting as is. And I think that's the greatest shame about him: the potential for something fascinating is there. There could be so much more to him. Add that complexity, however, and suddenly, he doesn't fit in the generic teenager's view as readily, and he'll be a less meaningful role model for more people.

…Then again, 012 is a terrible article as well, but I had to start a canon using it because the concept is so intriguing. We just need to find the way to similarly build out 049's mystique.

item.content:encoded:
I don't know why people say SCP-049 is "less mysterious" post-rewrite—all the mystery's still there (i.e. what the Pestilence is and how/whether he's curing it is still unknown), but he has an actual personality now, which adds even more dimension to the mystery.

They're probably focused on the mystery of who 049 is supposed to "be", instead of what he's doing. Which, yeah, the expanded interview logs of the rewrite mostly ruin by giving him a personality. 049-ARC is, metaphorically, more of a shadowy entity than the rewritten 049.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm glad this is here, because being able to directly point new users to the old 049 without telling them "okay scroll all the way down to the bottom of the article and open revisions and click view whichever" is neato—I wanted to show a friend the pre-rewrite SCP-049 and then post-rewrite SCP-049 and get an unbiased opinion on the differences, and this allows me to do so!

I love the rewrite. I don't know why people say SCP-049 is "less mysterious" post-rewrite—all the mystery's still there (i.e. what the Pestilence is and how/whether he's curing it is still unknown), but he has an actual personality now, which adds even more dimension to the mystery.

Like, if you read the old article, you'd assume he'd positively identified something he considers a disease, and believes zombifying people is the cure. The rewrite adds many more layers to it—like, is 049 mistaken about the Pestilence existing, but just too proud to admit it? Given how his interviewer suddenly became "sick", could there be an actual invisible disease that he can sense, and he's not crazy at all?

People who defend 049-ARC baffle me to the core, and IMO it stems from the more creepypasta-aligned offsite communities who aren't interested in anything that isn't ooky spooky grimdark mystery man, but that's just me projecting, probably.

Hate the rewrite audio logs, though. I think Volgun's emotionless death-rattle voice doesn't suit the more emotional, enthusiastic, trying-his-best 049 that we have now.
